S1.why: Invariable 'gratis' as a short label (12 max); the slots need no noun, the tiles are right above.

S2.why: An invitation to keep going, imperative in tu like the vocabulary's 'Attiva'; no limit or sales wording.

S3.s: Hai usato tutti i %lld cutling gratuiti. Restano gratis e funzionano come sempre.
S3.back: You-have used all the 5 cutling free. They-stay free and they-work as always.
S3.why: Lowercase invariable 'cutling' as in the vocabulary sentence; 'funzionano come sempre' is how an Italian says nothing changes.

S4.why: States the fact instead of 'Puoi salvare…', which reads like a manual; 'i primi' also hints that more can follow.

S5.why: 'X dei Y' reads right for any used count from 1 up; the numbers keep English order, so no positional forms are needed.

S6.why: Noun phrase as a row heading, 24 characters with '5.000'; 'cutling' stays invariable in the plural.

S7.s: Salva fino a %@ cutling di testo e %lld immagini.
S7.back: Save up to 5.000 cutling of text and 500 images.
S7.why: 'Cutling di testo' and 'immagini' are the vocabulary's own names for the two kinds.

S8.why: Italian joins the last of three with 'e' and no comma before it.

S9.s: Un solo acquisto vale su tutti e tre, con il tuo account Apple.
S9.back: One single purchase is-valid on all and three, with the your account Apple.
S9.why: 'Tutti e tre' ties it to the three devices above (bare 'tutti' would read as 'everyone'); 'account Apple' written as in the vocabulary.

S10.why: Second person present, the way a shop assistant would say it; 'una volta sola' stresses once more than 'una volta'.

S11.s: Niente abbonamento, niente pubblicità, niente registrazione.
S11.back: Nothing subscription, nothing advertising, nothing registration.
S11.why: The three things the brief names, each with colloquial 'niente'; 'registrazione' is the Italian word for signing up; 60 characters.

S12.why: The wording Italian iOS apps use for the App Store restore action.

S13.why: The usual Italian progress phrase, with the single ellipsis character.

S14.why: 'a' plus price is how an Italian shop states a price; 'tutto' matches S18, and S10 already says it is paid once.

S15.why: The same button without the price, 13 characters.

S16.why: The iOS Italian wording for putting something off politely, without refusing.

S17.why: The plain iOS Italian label for close buttons.

S18.why: Warm and short, tu form; 'tutto' takes in the room the grid has just shown.

S19.s: Grazie: con il tuo acquisto sostieni Cutling e l’unica persona che ci lavora.
S19.back: Thanks: with the your purchase you-support Cutling and the only person who on-it works.
S19.why: Thanks first, then what the purchase does; 'l'unica persona che ci lavora' avoids a gendered 'da solo/da sola'.

S20.s: Che piacere rivederti: il tuo acquisto è stato ripristinato.
S20.back: What pleasure to-see-you-again: the your purchase has been restored.
S20.why: 'Rivederti' greets a returning buyer without the gendered 'Bentornato/Bentornata'; 'ripristinato' echoes S12.

S21.why: Label then count, so VoiceOver reads it right for any count from 0 to 5; 'X di Y' is how Italian iOS reads a count out of a total.

S22.s: Cutling salvati: %lld. Ora c’è spazio per %@.
S22.back: Cutling saved: 5. Now there-is space for 5.000.
S22.why: Label plus number agrees for 1, 2, 5 and 21 alike, with no singular or plural ending to get wrong.

S23.s: Sbloccato. Ora hai spazio per %@ cutling.
S23.back: Unlocked. Now you-have space for 5.000 cutling.
S23.why: Leaves out the app's name so VoiceOver does not say 'Cutling' and 'cutling' back to back.

S24.why: A plain statement with no subject, so nobody is blamed.

S25.s: Impossibile connettersi all’App Store in questo momento. Riprova tra poco.
S25.back: Impossible to-connect to-the App Store in this moment. Try-again in a-little.
S25.why: 'Impossibile connettersi' is the usual Italian iOS phrasing; 'Riprova tra poco' gives the way out.

S26.s: L’App Store non ha confermato questo acquisto.
S26.back: The App Store not has confirmed this purchase.
S26.why: The App Store is the subject, so the person is not blamed.

S27.s: Non risultano acquisti di Cutling sull’account Apple di questo dispositivo.
S27.back: Not result purchases of Cutling on-the account Apple of this device.
S27.why: 'Non risultano' is the natural Italian for 'nothing on record'; 'account Apple' and 'dispositivo' as in the vocabulary sentence.

S28.s: Nella versione gratuita c’è posto per %lld cutling. Sblocca Cutling una volta e salvane quanti vuoi.
S28.back: In-the version free there-is room for 5 cutling. Unlock Cutling one time and save-of-them as-many-as you-want.
S28.why: Spoken as Siri would say it; 'salvane quanti vuoi' is the everyday way to say 'as many as you like'.

S29.why: A quota label fitting in 18 characters; it sits under the list title, so 'cutling' is implied.

K1.s: Finiti i %lld gratis. Tocca per sbloccare
K1.back: Finished the 5 free. Tap to unlock
K1.why: Short and spoken, 38 characters; 'Tocca per…' is the usual Italian iOS call to tap.

M1.why: Leads with an imperative verb, like Italian Mac window and menu commands.

M2.why: The same command as M1, with the ellipsis character because it opens a window.

M3.why: Row label using the vocabulary's word; its value M4 gives the count.

M4.why: The compact 'X di Y' pair that Italian Apple software uses.

M5.why: Reads as a row status on its own; masculine agreement with the app's name.

M6.s: Con un solo acquisto sblocchi Cutling su iPhone, iPad e Mac.
M6.back: With one single purchase you-unlock Cutling on iPhone, iPad and Mac.
M6.why: Same three-device list as S8; tu form.

M7.s: Sbloccato su iPhone, iPad e Mac con questo account Apple.
M7.back: Unlocked on iPhone, iPad and Mac with this account Apple.
M7.why: Subject left out after the section title Cutling; 'account Apple' written as in the vocabulary.

M8.s: Hai comprato Cutling prima che fosse gratis: resta sbloccato. Grazie di averci creduto.
M8.back: You-have bought Cutling before that it-were free: it-stays unlocked. Thanks of having-in-it believed.
M8.why: Subjunctive 'fosse' after 'prima che' as a native writes it; 'averci creduto' thanks an early buyer without gendered endings.
